we developed a deep learning model that detects early coronary artery occlusions with high accuracy, and that this is the first time that a deep learning approach has been shown to detect early coronary artery occlusive disease with high sensitivity and specificity.

a convolutional neural network can detect ischaemic ECGs with a higher balance of sensitivity and specific than existing methods, and that this model is capable of detecting ischaemic EGCs that are missed by expert cardiologists.

we have developed an artificial intelligence model for the detection of early acute coronary artery occlusions from 12 lead ECGs, that has better sensitivity than the current standard, and that is as good as expert human interpretation.

developing a deep learning model that can detect early ischaemia from 12 lead ECG recordings.
augmenting expert detection of acute ischaemia from ECG.

the deep learning model is a useful adjunct to expert interpretation, but not a replacement.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep learning can augment expert cardiologists in detecting early coronary artery occlusions from 12-lead ECG recordings.

we have demonstrated that a deep learning algorithm is able to detect ischaemia in ECGs with a better balance in terms of sensitivity and specificity compared to existing STE criteria or computerised analysers, and that it is able to detect the same number of ischaemic ECGs as expert cardiologists, while having a better sensitivity.
deep learning can be used as an adjunct to STE criteria for the detection of ischaemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning models can improve expert performance by augmenting expert interpretation, and that this is particularly relevant to clinical problems where expert sensitivity is low.
deep learning can be used to improve the detection of early acute coronary artery occlusions from 12 lead ECGs.
